name: Pedestrian Semantic Segmentation
description: The Pedestrian Semantic Segmentation dataset pairs urban street images with natural language prompts instructing the segmentation of pedestrians, and provides pixel-level ground-truth masks. It evaluates text-guided image semantic segmentation in driving scenes.
card_text: This dataset consists of 160 samples from urban driving scenes (Cityscapes-style). Each sample includes an RGB image (input.image_file), a short text prompt (input.prompt) such as 'Segment out the pedestrian in the image', and a corresponding ground-truth label ID mask (output.map_file) that encodes pixel-level semantic classes. The images show complex street scenes with multiple objects; the prompt specifies the target class to segment. The mask uses integer label IDs for all classes, including the pedestrian class. The task requires the model to produce a segmentation map that correctly segments the instructed class. Assumptions: images and masks are spatially aligned, labels follow a fixed ID scheme, and the prompt is a direct segmentation instruction.

image.semantics: The input RGB image shows an urban street scene from a driving perspective, typically containing pedestrians and other objects; it serves as the visual input that the model must segment.

question.semantics: A short natural language instruction that tells the model which object class to segment (e.g., 'Segment out the pedestrian in the image').

mask.semantics: The ground-truth semantic segmentation mask corresponding to the input image, stored as a label ID PNG. It provides pixel-level class annotations, including the pedestrian category, and serves as the target output for the segmentation task.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of an input object with an image_file path and a text prompt instructing pedestrian segmentation, and an output object with a map_file path to the corresponding ground-truth label ID mask. The image and mask are spatially aligned; the prompt defines the target category for the pixel-level segmentation. No additional structured fields are present.
